💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S.
  • Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.
  • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the ongoing earnings season, Middle East tensions and buzz ahead of the U.S. midterm elections have been keeping investors busy. Further, worries about elevated artificial intelligence spending are weighing on investor sentiment.

Investors looking beyond the short-term noise and focusing on long-term returns can track top Wall Street analysts to pick the right stocks, backed by strong research.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

This week's first stock pick is Datadog, an AI-powered observability and security platform. The company will announce its results for the third quarter on Nov. 4. Datadog is seeing strong demand for its offerings, thanks to cloud migration and rapid AI adoption. TipRanks' KPIs tool for DDOG shows the growth in its customer base over the past few years amid increasing market penetration and growing adoption of its products.

Heading into Q3 FY26 earnings, Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda reiterated a buy rating on Datadog stock and raised his price target to $335 from $305. The analyst noted that industry checks and data indicate that infrastructure software demand is strengthening, with AI increasingly driving usage and growth.

It has been revealed that ikeda called Datadog and Atlassian his top picks, saying that companies that can show that AI is a tailwind to growth could see their valuation rerate, even at premium multiples. He added that the total addressable market for observability is growing faster than anticipated, driven by accelerated growth of enterprise AI and the rapid ramp of consumer AI agents.

It has been revealed that the five-star analyst believes that focus will be on revenue growth, which he estimates to be 28.7% for Q3 FY26 versus the Street's consensus of 29.1%. Ikeda thinks that the market is underestimating the growth prospects of DDOG's security products. Meanwhile, he cautioned investors about concentration risk related to large customers.

"We think results will be supportive of our long-term thesis that Datadog is a strong share gainer in the rapidly expanding observability opportunity," mentioned Ikeda.

According to recent reports, ikeda ranks No. 673 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 55% of the time, delivering an average return of 10.9%. See Datadog Statistics on TipRanks.

The next pick, semiconductor giant Nvidia, is also benefiting from AI-driven demand for its products. After attending Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reaffirmed a buy rating on NVDA stock with a price target of $300, calling it a top pick in the semiconductor space.

It has been revealed that the five-star analyst noted that the conference supported his thesis that Nvidia continues to effectively navigate bottlenecks in the supply chain, land/power/shell, and funding. In fact, Moore is "convinced that all 3 aspects are opportunities for NVDA.".

While Nvidia's GTC Berlin offered no major updates, Moore noted the conference reflected that the firm continues to add to its significant advantages heading into 2027. The analyst mentioned that Vera Rubin is gaining momentum, though details on next year's Rubin Ultra were lighter than expected.

With demand outpacing supply, Moore noted that focus is on closing the gap. In this regard, he highlighted the supply chain deals on substrate, packaging and testing. While the analyst continues to view TSMC 3 nm wafer supply as the biggest challenge, he expects it to ease over time.

Recent findings suggest that moore ranks No. 142 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 59% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.4%. See Nvidia Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Aerospace organization SpaceX recently unveiled solid third-quarter results, with its AI revenue surging to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the prior-year quarter.

Impressed by the results, Needham analyst Ryan Koontz reiterated a buy rating on SPCX stock with a price target of $250. Koontz highlighted that SpaceX's Q3 results significantly exceeded expectations, proving that the organization's vertically integrated business model is driving massive scale.

Sources indicate that furthermore, Koontz emphasized the 195.2% sequential growth in SpaceX's AI revenue, fueled by wholesale spot compute deals. He noted management's increasing focus on its AI strategy, given that it is optimistic about adding 10 gigawatts of incremental capacity during 2027.

"With increasing confidence on Starship re-use, we meaningfully increase our estimates," stated Koontz.

Koontz ranks No. 357 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 42% of the time, delivering an average return of 23.7%. See SpaceX Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    Goldman Sachs Sees 52 More GW of Data Center Power in 2028. These 3 Stocks Look Best Positioned to Cash In.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (808 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is rapidly running into a hard physical constraint: electricity.
    • data center power capacity and demand have already climbed nearly 30% year-to-date, accounting for more than one-third of the country's total electricity demand growth.
    • What's fueling this demand, and which stocks could win?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neha Chamaria – Nov 25, 2026 at 2:06PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Recent findings suggest that the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is rapidly running into a hard physical constraint: electricity. In a research note cited by Reuters, Goldman Sachs (GS -0.62%) projected that up to 52 gigawatts (GW) of additional data center power capacity could come online in the U.S. through 2028.

    Goldman noted that U.S. data center power capacity and demand have already climbed nearly 30% year-to-date, accounting for more than one-third of the country's total electricity demand growth. It expects natural gas consumption to rise and is bullish on gas prices.

    What's fueling this demand, and which stocks could win?

    AI data centers need 24/7 stable, uninterrupted power, even when the sun sets or the wind dies down. That gives an edge to power sources that can run on demand, and natural gas is the biggest of them.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2025, natural gas made up 40% of U.S. utility-scale generating capacity, compared with 31.5% for all renewables combined and 13.3% for coal, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. When Texas set its all-time demand record on July 22, 2026, gas supplied 48% of the power and solar supplied 32%.

    Sources indicate that speed matters too, as hyperscalers and data center operators can't wait years for a grid connection. Delays are costly. At an event in October, Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) CEO Jensen Huang estimated that a 1-gigawatt AI data center can generate around $40 billion a year in revenue, and a three-month delay pushes back roughly $10 billion in revenue.

    That urgency makes reliable fuel and fast power delivery critical, pushing developers toward natural gas. Three stocks could cash in, as they span the entire power value chain.

    Energy Transfer (ET +0.70%), which sits along major natural gas corridors supplying power generation and industrial demand. It owns and operates nearly 140,000 miles of pipeline infrastructure, connecting major producing basins and markets.

    Since the start of 2025, Energy Transfer has signed more than 9.5 million MMBtu (one million British thermal units) per day of agreements with hyperscalers, data centers, and power plants. These include agreements with Oracle (ORCL -5.13%) for three data centers, two of which are in Texas.

    The company indicates it is in "advanced negotiations" with multiple customers to supply natural gas along its pipeline network, which includes Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Ohio, Louisiana, and Illinois. These are also among the largest data center markets today.

    TXSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Its new Hugh Brinson Pipeline entered full service in September ahead of schedule and carries Permian gas about 400 miles to the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

    Recent findings suggest that energy Transfer earns primarily under long-term fee-based agreements and pays a steady, growing dividend. The stock yields 7.3%.

    Recent findings suggest that bloom Energy (BE -2.25%) directly targets the power bottleneck by making solid-oxide fuel cells that provide modular, on-site power at facilities. Its fuel cells generally run on natural gas today, and growth has been explosive.

    According to recent reports, third-quarter revenue surged 138.1% to a record $1.2 billion, with fuel cell system sales surpassing $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time. Bloom raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the third time in the year, projecting 122% growth. Management didn't give backlog numbers, but said it is growing faster than revenue.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Bloom Energy has secured massive partnerships, including a $25 billion financing deal with global asset management giant Brookfield Asset Management (BAM +2.60%).

    GE Vernova (GEV -0.78%) makes large gas turbines, and almost 25% of all the electricity generated globally passes through its equipment. It also makes high-voltage transformers, switchgear, and control systems needed to connect data centers and buildings with the transmission lines.

    According to recent reports, while the industry lead times for some of these equipment now stretch into years, turbine buyers are paying up to book factory slots through 2032. Its latest agreement to acquire Trench Group for $9 billion is a calculated move to vertically integrate and secure parts supplies for transformers and other equipment.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    CEO Scott Strazik remarked full-year 2026 order pricing per kilowatt is on track to rise 50% from last year. With higher prices and volumes, you should expect bigger sales, margins, cash flows, and returns on capital.

    #108135. Tech Report: 19 Business Upgrades To Maximize The Value Of Real-Time Payments

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1316 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: 19 Business Upgrades To Maximize The Value Of Real-Time Payments

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1316 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As instant-payment networks such as FedNow and the RTP network reach more financial institutions, more businesses have the opportunity to send and receive funds within seconds, even on weekends and holidays.
    • For many companies, the transition to real-time payments will require a fresh look at the internal technology and business practices that support financial operations.
    • Industry observers note that update ERP payment reconciliation and the capacity behind it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As instant-payment networks such as FedNow and the RTP network reach more financial institutions, more businesses have the opportunity to send and receive funds within seconds, even on weekends and holidays. However, taking full advantage of that speed requires more than gaining access to a new payment network. Legacy workflows built around batch processing and traditional banking hours can create delays and operational gaps even when money moves instantly.

    For many companies, the transition to real-time payments will require a fresh look at the internal technology and business practices that support financial operations. Below, Forbes Technology Council members share ways companies can modernize their systems and processes to make real-time payments more efficient, secure and beneficial to the business.

    Industry observers note that update ERP payment reconciliation and the capacity behind it. From my experience leading fintech integration projects, connecting payment channels is only part of the work. Internal systems must confirm transactions, update balances and flag duplicates at any hour. Adopt API-driven, automated reconciliation with exception handling, and load-test it at peak volume without maintenance windows. - Mohammad Sharif Daoud, Global Center for AI Excellence.

    Industry observers note that combine automated matching with clear ownership of exceptions. Routine transactions should reconcile automatically, while unmatched payments, short payments and missing remittance details are routed to accountable teams for timely resolution. This approach reduces manual effort, improves visibility into available cash, and helps finance teams put incoming funds to work sooner while resolving discrepancies faster. - Venus Garg, Elevance Health.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Providers and participants in the expanding instant payments ecosystem must modernize risk assessment alongside payment infrastructure. Instant settlement leaves little room for error, while added verification and manual review undermine speed. Richer financial data and streamlined fraud, liquidity and other risk assessments can enable more instant payments without sacrificing sound controls. - Brian Reshefsky, EDGE.

    Recent findings suggest that companies should modernize their treasury and cash management systems. Real-time payments mean little if reconciliation, liquidity management and reporting remain outdated. Integrating automation, AI-driven forecasting and real-time financial visibility enables businesses to optimize cash flow, reduce risk and make faster, smarter capital decisions. - Paul Kerslake, N3XUS.

    Sources indicate that payment routing deserves more attention. Many companies choose how to send money based on fixed bank relationships or manual processes. Connecting internal systems to multiple payment networks lets them route each payment based on cost, availability and whether the recipient can receive it instantly. That makes real-time payments useful across the business instead of within a single network. - Maghnus Mareneck, Cosmos Labs.

    I’d modernize how procurement negotiates supplier payment terms. If a company can pay immediately upon verified delivery, procurement should be able to negotiate something in return, such as a discount, better pricing or priority access to inventory. That requires procurement and finance to agree on when using cash sooner is worthwhile. The opportunity is to make payment speed part of the negotiation. - Kacee Johnson, radical.

    Industry observers note that fraud detection and payment authorization need to evolve with real-time payments. When money moves instantly, there’s little time to detect fraud or reverse a transaction. Companies need real-time fraud analysis and stronger verification that a payment was genuinely authorized by the customer, without slowing down legitimate transactions. - Alex Spokoiny, Check Point Software.

    Recent findings suggest that patch cash and liquidity management. When payments settle around the clock, including weekends, treasury can’t rely on end-of-day positions and cutoff times. Modernize to real-time cash visibility and automated funding of accounts so you can pay and collect any time without tying up idle balances. - Aruna Veerappan, Upwork Global Inc.

    Customer-facing billing and refund workflows should be modernized to take full advantage of real-time payments. Many companies still rely on multi-day settlement, batch disbursements and manual refund processes that frustrate customers accustomed to instant transactions. Modernized workflows deliver instant payouts, real-time refunds and transparent payment status, improving customer experience and loyalty. - Nitin Agarwal, Luminace.

    Companies should modernize how they track incoming payments. What’s the point of receiving money in seconds if accounting takes two days to recognize it? It’s like getting a package delivered instantly but waiting until tomorrow to open the door. Real-time payments need real-time accounting. - Margarita Simonova, ILoveMyQA.

    Industry observers note that companies should modernize their payment approval workflows to keep pace with instant-payment networks. If a supplier payment still waits until the next business day for approval, the money may move instantly, but the business hasn’t gained much. Setting approval limits and delegating authority in advance lets routine payments go through around the clock, while larger or unusual transactions still get reviewed before funds leave the account. - Elton Chan, Second Talent.

    Modernize the payment decisioning and exception-management architecture. Real-time settlement atop batch-era fraud controls, liquidity monitoring, reconciliation and exception handling merely accelerates operational risk. 24/7 money movement demands 24/7 intelligence, controls and accountability. Speed without trust is a liability. - Rajjie Sarmey, FutureProof CXO™.

    Recent findings suggest that companies should modernize their liquidity orchestration layer, not just payment gateways. Real-time payments require real-time intelligence across treasury, fraud detection, reconciliation and cash forecasting. The next frontier is agentic liquidity management, where AI continuously anticipates cash needs, dynamically allocates funds and optimizes working capital. Instant settlement should enable instant financial decisions. - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    It has been revealed that real-time payments won’t automatically create value. I’d challenge the premise that modernizing one process or internal system is enough. Companies need to assess technical debt, process debt and data debt together. Money can move instantly while the business operates on yesterday’s information. The question leaders need to focus on is whether the entire organization can access and act on that data. - Neda Nia, Stibo Systems.

    Sources indicate that modernize how you approve and double-check payouts before money goes out the door. Older payment methods gave finance teams until the end of the day to catch a duplicate invoice, a wrong account or a bad refund before the bank processed it. With instant payments, the money is gone in seconds, so your approval rules and mistake checks have to happen up front, before anyone clicks “Send.” - Vatsal Bhardwaj, Jabali.ai.

    Recent findings suggest that revision collections and customer communication. If payment status reaches the CRM overnight, customers who paid at 9 a.m. still get an overdue reminder at noon. At one client, about one in 10 dunning emails went to accounts that had already paid. Streaming payment events into Salesforce stopped those messages, cut “I already paid” support cases by roughly 35%, and released credit holds the same day. - Sergii Grushai, Peeklogic.

    Modernize tax determination and allocation. When a customer pays instantly, the manufacturer should reserve sales tax, VAT and withholding by jurisdiction and legal entity. Many firms calculate these obligations later from batch reports, overstating available cash and rushing remittances. Link payment events to tax rules and entity records, then test reversals and partial payments so speed does not create a compliance backlog. This clearly separates cash from tax owed. - Jagadish Gokavarapu, Wissen Infotech.

    Sources indicate that your customer service layer needs modernization. Here’s why: Real-time payments are final. There’s no recall window. So the “Here’s my money, can I cancel it?” questions spike, and they need answers in seconds, not tomorrow. In our banking data, payments and money movement drive roughly 36% of guided-task volume. Instant money needs instant, accurate answers. - Merlin Bise, Inbenta.

    Companies should integrate instant-payment networks directly with their ERP or through treasury platforms, ensuring cash inflows and outflows are reflected in real time. Payment initiation, status updates, and automated AR and AP matching can enable straight-through processing, reduce manual intervention and improve cash visibility. This aligns financial operations with payment speed, improving efficiency and working capital management. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

    Abercrombie & Fitch Grew Sales for the 16th Straight Quarter as Earnings Jumped 62%. Here's What's Behind the Streak.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Abercrombie & Fitch ›.
    • Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF +5.27%) set a fresh record and extended an impressive winning streak in its third quarter.
    • Recent findings suggest that while not every one of the quarter's many growth figures was as remarkable as it looked, there's no denying the power of the aforementioned streak.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 25, 2026 at 2:16PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Abercrombie & Fitch ›.

    Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF +5.27%) set a fresh record and extended an impressive winning streak in its third quarter. So it was little wonder that investors couldn't wait to pounce on the stock following the earnings announcement Tuesday morning. On the back of that demand, it closed the trading day nearly 20% higher in price.

    Recent findings suggest that while not every one of the quarter's many growth figures was as remarkable as it looked, there's no denying the power of the aforementioned streak. Read on for more about the clothing retailer's memorable third frame, and how it extended that already-long run.

    The latest all-time high Abercrombie set was third-quarter net sales, which in the 2026 version rocketed 11% higher year over year to $1.4 billion. It didn't hesitate to mention that this was no less than the 16th consecutive quarter of growth. This was powered by both of the tech giant's leading brand families, its namesake Abercrombie & Fitch, whose sales rose by 12%, and Hollister, up 11%. Meanwhile, the company's overall comparable sales notched an impressive, though smaller, 6% gain.

    Equity analysts had underestimated Abercrombie. On average, they were modeling net sales of $1.37 billion.

    Industry observers note that as for profitability, attributable net income climbed by a meaty 45% to over $164 million, or $3.82 per share. The company emphasized that the latter figure represented a 62% year-over-year increase. Yet some of this was due to a sharp reduction in share count; the weighted-average basic shares outstanding figure for the quarter was almost 42.3 million, compared with third-quarter 2025's 46.8 million-plus. That's because Abercrombie replenished its stock repurchase program last March, with its board authorizing a massive $1.3 billion for the purpose. Ever since, it has been steadily executing on that initiative.

    According to recent reports, another factor to consider when examining the tech giant's bottom line is the impact of tariff refunds. During the quarter, it was reimbursed by the federal government for duties it paid under a set of 2025 tariffs that were later ruled illegal by the Supreme Court. This added $0.40 to the company's per-share net income figure. Adjusting profitability by that amount reduces it to $3.42, bringing the year-over-year improvement down to "only" 45%.

    That figure still crushes the consensus analyst projection of $3.09. In other words, while tariffs made a bit of difference to profitability, Abercrombie did smashingly well in the quarter regardless.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that abercrombie's fashion is, as ever, geared toward younger consumers. It blankets that demographic rather well, with the Abercrombie & Fitch brand group targeting older, theoretically more choosy and sophisticated customers, and the relatively casual Hollister lines aimed at their younger counterparts.

    According to recent reports, both manage to stay in fashion and on the wish list of such people, buttressed by clever marketing. When a clothing tech giant's wares are in vogue, it has less of a need to discount them (a common practice in the business). In its earnings release, Abercrombie also pointed to good discipline in its inventory management as a secret to its third-quarter success. Hence the double-digit improvements in both sales and profitability.

    Recent findings suggest that the timing of this is fortuitous, because the consumer discretionary sector is entering the eternally important holiday season. With its considerable growth momentum, the tech giant felt confident enough to raise its annual guidance for the second quarter in a row.

    In a recent development, it's now modeling sales growth of 6% over the 2025 result, up from the preceding prediction of 5%. EPS should come in at $13.70 to $13.90, encouragingly above the former range of $13.10 to $13.60. Management maintained its projection for the impact of tariff refunds; these should add 220 basis points to its operating margin. Guidance for yearly spend on those share-count-reducing stock buybacks was also kept level, at $500 million.

    Industry observers note that sales growth streaks are hard to achieve and often harder to maintain. That goes double for the ever-fickle retail fashion industry. But if any company's going to keep one alive, it's Abercrombie, which always seems to have its finger on the pulse of what its youthful customers like to wear. I'd be a buyer of this stock, particularly considering its modest forward P/E of 12.5, even after Tuesday's monster pop.

    Although Lucid stock is slightly less expensive today than earlier in the week, investors should hold off before rushing to load up. The company's inability to generate organic cash flow -- something that doesn't seem likely to change anytime soon -- means that this stock is best left to those comfortable with more speculative investments. At this point, most investors are better suited watching Lucid stock from the side of the road for the time being.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
    • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    It has been revealed that but enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Recent findings suggest that ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    Industry observers note that arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

    Champions 🏆 pic.twitter.com/c0IVLYu3fB.

    Industry observers note that arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

    Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

    Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

    The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

    Industry observers note that meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

    We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

    A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

    He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

    Sources indicate that another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

    There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

    Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

    Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

    Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

    The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

    There will now be a penalty shootout.

    There will be three added minutes.

    It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

    There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

    Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

    Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:.

    Industry observers note that with just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

    In a recent development, the Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

    Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

    Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

    Sources indicate that in the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

    Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

    Sources indicate that arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

    Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

    Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

    Sources indicate that that is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

    White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

    In a recent development, dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

    Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

    We are back under way at the Emirates.

    During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

    Recent findings suggest that konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o.

    The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

    Industry observers note that gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

    Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

    Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

    According to recent reports, after Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

    Industry observers note that arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

    Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

    Sources indicate that tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

    Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

    Industry observers note that with it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

    What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

    It has been revealed that odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

    Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

    In a recent development, A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

    Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

    Industry observers note that should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

    According to recent reports, odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

    Recent findings suggest that gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

    Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

    Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

    In a recent development, the German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,.

    In a recent development, dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

    Sources indicate that gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

    Walmart+ Members Spend 4 Times As Much As Non-Members. The Retailer’s Newly introduced $120 Bundle Could Unlock More Growth.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that for most of the industry's existence, retailing was simply a matter of offering the right product at the right price in the right place at the right time.
    • The internet has changed the increasingly competitive retailing landscape, however.
    • According to recent reports, walmart's (WMT -0.32%) ecosystem just got a serious upgrade.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Brumley – Nov 25, 2026 at 2:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Walmart ›.

    Industry observers note that for most of the industry's existence, retailing was simply a matter of offering the right product at the right price in the right place at the right time. Shoppers would find your store, and gladly give you their money.

    The internet has changed the increasingly competitive retailing landscape, however. People are empowered, with access to many choices. Simply opening a store's doors isn't enough. In this environment, the key is building an ecosystem that makes your stores the top-of-mind choice for meeting consumers' shopping needs.

    According to recent reports, walmart's (WMT -0.32%) ecosystem just got a serious upgrade. Investors should take note, as it offers some much-needed growth potential.

    According to recent reports, in October, Walmart combined the benefits of Walmart+ (like free shipping) with membership in its club-based warehouse retailer Sam's Club. Subscriptions that individually would normally cost $98 and $60 per year, respectively, can now be combined for an annual cost of only $120.

    The real opportunity with this offering, however, is a chance to poach some of the affluent paying members of Sam's Club's rival Costco Wholesale (COST -0.45%).

    Recent findings suggest that walmart was already doing pretty well with this crowd, to be clear. With even higher-earning households feeling the pinch of lingering inflation, most of the company's market share gains since 2022 have come from America's more affluent households.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that the proverbial prize here, however, is a portion of Costco's 84.1 million paid memberships. Costco's average member lives in a household with an average annual income of over $100,000. The typical Walmart customer's comparable income is just over half that amount.

    Sam's Club alone isn't apt to encourage much defection. If Walmart can add value to its Sam's Club offering by adding the convenience of Walmart stores' wider and less-bulk inventory selection at an annual price in the ballpark of Costco's membership fees, it's got a chance of winning over at least some of these coveted higher-spending customers.

    The average Costco member spends about $3,000 per year, by the way, versus roughly half that for Sam's Club members, and just a little more than that for the average Walmart store customer.

    Most Costco members aren't apt to make such a switch, to be clear. However, it wouldn't take many defectors to make a noticeable difference in Walmart's top and bottom lines, now that paid access to both sets of perks is affordably accessible.

    3 Glorious AI Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist If the Stock Market Crashes

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that crashes may feel scary for investors, but they're also the best time to buy certain stocks.
    • Sources indicate that the stock market falls by at least 10% around once every 16 months, on average, according to Hartford Funds.
    • In a recent development, we could have already passed the bottom of one of those typical corrections, or we could still be near the start of a bigger decline: No one knows.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By John Ballard – Nov 25, 2026 at 2:42PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    Recent findings suggest that crashes may feel scary for investors, but they're also the best time to buy certain stocks. Companies that provide essential services, earn substantial profits, and have ample cash on their books can keep investing through downturns. The strongest companies often come out of a downturn stronger than they went in.

    Sources indicate that the stock market falls by at least 10% around once every 16 months, on average, according to Hartford Funds. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) recently closed 11.6% below its Oct. 6 record high on Nov. 20 and at the moment sits about 8% below that high. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, is still down by about 14% from its recent peak.

    In a recent development, we could have already passed the bottom of one of those typical corrections, or we could still be near the start of a bigger decline: No one knows. But if the market falls further, Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%)(GOOG -2.02%), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -1.96%), and Amazon (AMZN -3.12%) would be artificial intelligence (AI) stocks worth buying. Here's why.

    Alphabet is the company behind Google Search, YouTube, and the Gemini AI model. Billions of people use its products. Search is how much of the world finds information online, and YouTube is a go-to destination for video. And the Gemini app now has 1 billion users.

    In a recent development, that reach allows Alphabet to rake in substantial advertising revenue across its platforms. Google Services, which includes Search, YouTube, and subscriptions, generated $96 billion in revenue in the third quarter and earned about $0.41 of operating profit per dollar of sales. A recession might cause advertising spending to decline, slowing Alphabet's revenue growth. Still, the massive reach of its services business means the manufacturer should see its revenue march higher over the long term.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In a recent development, moreover, AI appears to be enhancing its long-term growth prospects. Alphabet noted Search queries grew at their fastest pace in five years last quarter. That matters because earlier in the generative AI revolution, many investors and analysts feared that users asking AI chatbots questions would lead to a reduction in traffic to Google Search.

    The stock trades at about 18 times next year's earnings estimates, in line with the S&P 500, which also trades at about that ratio, while analysts expect Alphabet’s earnings to grow about 17% annually. If a broader market crash took the tech stock down with it, that would turn a market leader trading at a fair price into a bargain.

    Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is the world's leading contract chipmaker. Its foundries physically produce the chips designed by other companies, including almost all cutting-edge AI processors. When companies need the most advanced chips in large quantities, TSMC is the partner they turn to, because no rival has its massive production capacity or manufacturing expertise.

    That position gives TSMC pricing power. Its operating margin was 59% last quarter, meaning it kept about $0.59 of every dollar of sales as operating profit. Management expects revenue to grow by about 44% in U.S. dollars this year as demand for AI chips continues to climb.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The biggest risk to the company is geopolitical. Most of TSMC's leading-edge factories are in Taiwan, and a conflict involving China could disrupt its chip production.

    Recent findings suggest that but that's why TSMC is working to expand its foundry operations geographically. Its fresh manufacturing facility in Arizona is expected to begin volume production in the third quarter of 2027. The company is also evaluating expansion in Texas, which would help mitigate this risk over the long term.

    Industry observers note that trading at about 15.5 times next year's expected earnings, below the market's roughly 18 times, the stock looks undervalued. Analysts expect about 44% annualized earnings growth in the coming years. A further drop in the share price would make the stock a steal.

    Amazon runs a massive online store, an advertising business, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), its cloud platform. It just posted its highest operating margin ever, nearly 14% in the third quarter. Cash from operations rose 19% year over year to $42 billion in Q3, and grew by 29% to $168 billion over the last 12 months.

    Industry observers note that amazon Bedrock, the AWS service that lets businesses run AI models, saw token volume (a key measure of AI usage) grow nearly 17 times year over year. This makes Amazon one of the best stocks for the average investor to profit from enterprise AI adoption, since AWS generates most of Amazon's profit.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    The stock's valuation is not as low as the others. At about 23 times 2027 earnings, it trades at a premium to the market, yet analysts expect earnings to grow roughly 23% annually. Softer demand for cloud services could send the stock lower. That's the risk, but a sluggish year of growth wouldn't derail the organization's long-term trajectory.

    Industry observers note that amazon's margins are trending higher, and rising cash from operations would let it keep investing in growth through a downturn. A market crash wouldn’t keep tens of millions of people from shopping on Amazon.com, nor would it stop enterprises from needing to store their data on AWS. It would only bring the stock's valuation down to more attractive levels, making it potentially a bargain for patient investors.

    It has been revealed that that's a forward annual dividend yield of around 2.8%. However, this is far from the only long-term economic return you can receive from investing in McDonald's. McDonald’s shares trade for around 20 times forward earnings, while faster-growing consumer staples blue chips, like Coca-Cola, trade for over 25 times forward earnings. During the third quarter of 2026, the bank continued to operate in a dynamic macroeconomic environment marked by some short-term challenges, including a moderation in economic activity, inflation above initial expectations, and a more gradual evolution of loans and deposits than originally anticipated. Nevertheless, we remain confident in the medium and long-term outlook for the Argentine economy, supported by ongoing structural reforms and deregulation, solid financial and fiscal fundamentals, positive developments in the trade balance, and increasing investment opportunities.

    Recent findings suggest that we believe these factors are the laying foundations for a more stable, predictable, and sustainable economic environment, creating favorable conditions for the continued development and growth of our business. In this context, BBVA continues to strengthen its competitive positioning, consolidating its place as the second-largest private bank, leading financial intermediation growth among its main peers in a challenging credit quality landscape. Moving on to our financial highlights for the quarter, BBVA Argentina posted an inflation-adjusted net income of ARS 58.9 billion for the third quarter of 2026. This represents a 57.7% decrease quarter-over-quarter and a quarterly ROE of 4.9%.

    Sources indicate that the decline was mainly driven by a decrease in net interest margins stemmed from interest rates dropping compared to the first half of the year, which negatively affected asset repricing and also from lower yields on inflation-adjusted assets. As a consequence, NIMs declined from 18.2% to 15.1% in the quarter. It is worth mentioning that NIM adjusted by inflation cost, which in our view best reflects the evolution of margin over time, fell 260 basis points in the quarter to 12.2% and 10 basis points compared to 12 months ago, even with liabilities rate level approximately 2,000 basis points lower.

    Regarding efficiency, our quarterly efficiency ratio stood at 49.6%, mainly affected by lower operating income, while personnel benefits and administrative expenses still proved a better performance. Nonetheless, year-to-date results show a positive overview, with a net income of nine months of ARS 294.4 billion, 14.4% above the same period in 2025. These figures arise from a 16% growth in net interest margin, a 17% improvement in net fee income, and a 6% reduction in personnel and administrative expenses, which, although largely offset by a 44% increase in loan loss allowances, lets us glimpse the potential of the business if credit situation continues to normalize as expected. Now, let's look at the dynamics of our balance sheet and credit portfolio.

    Total financing to the private sector closed the quarter at ARS 18.4 trillion, increasing 2% quarter-over-quarter. While local currency loans increased 0.8%, our foreign currency private loans grew by 5.6% sequentially, equivalent to a 9.2% increase in hard currency. On the retail side, mortgage lending continues to gain momentum alongside pledge loans. Furthermore, we are successfully capturing business, mainly driven by the commercial segment and foreign currency loans. Our consolidated loan market share stood at 11.93%, signaling a total gain of 40 basis points over the last 12 months. On the funding side, total deposits reached ARS 19.8 trillion. Private deposit market share increased from 9.90% to 10.22% in the quarter, and up 14 basis points year-over-year.

    According to recent reports, in terms of asset quality, we are beginning to observe favorable signs in portfolio evolution, particularly in early delinquency indicators. This improvement is progressively reflected in lower loan loss allowances, which recorded a 5% decrease in real terms during the period, although there is still room for a more significant reduction. BBVA's NPL ratio at the end of September was 5.55%, a 54 basis point decrease quarter-over-quarter, while the system presented a ratio of 7.4% as of August, last available data as of the moment of this recording. Cost of risk shows a similar decline from 7.13% in the second quarter of 2026 to 6.58% in the third quarter of 2026.

    Looking at solvency and liquidity, our liquidity ratio closed at a very comfortable 44.4%. More importantly, our capital position remains robust, with a regulatory capital ratio of 17.9%, representing 117.6% excess over minimum regulatory requirements. For subsequent periods, our expectation is to consolidate an upward path in profits once again, driven by progressive improvement in risk indicators and intermediation margins within a context of expense control. In this context, we continue to strengthen our capabilities to capture opportunities that arise when the economic cycle regains momentum, creating value for our stakeholders, clients, investors, and the country's productive development. Thank you for your time and continued support.

    I would like now to turn the call over to Carmen Morillo, our CFO, for some closing remarks.

Over the last few years, we have achieved significant scale, with a market share of around 12% in lending and above 10% in deposits. We are now in a very good position to build on that scale. Our priority is to make the most of it by deepening customer relationships, increasing transactional activity, and improving profitability.

    It has been revealed that in retail, we continue to focus on secured lending, particularly mortgages and auto loans, and customers where we have greater visibility and repayment capability. On the corporate side, we see interesting opportunities in the more dynamic sectors of the economy and across their value chains. Our expectations for loan growth for this year is now more moderate, reflecting the slower recovery in demand. As economic activity and real incomes recover, we expect lending to gradually regain momentum, always with a focus on profitability and asset quality. Moving to margins, lower interest rates have put pressure on asset yields, but going forward, we expect margins to remain stable.

    However, in Argentina, it is key to look at the margins and inflation together. As inflation comes down, the negative impact of inflation accounting in our results should also decrease, partially offsetting the pressure that lower interest rates have had on the net interest income. Our focus remains on pricing, funding mix, and business volumes. On fees, despite a weaker quarter due to some specific reasons, we have achieved solid growth of around 17% year-to-date in real terms compared to last year. Going forward, we want transactional activity to become an increasingly important source of revenues. On asset quality, we are starting to see the improvement in early arrears that we mentioned last quarter reflected in our NPL ratio.

    We have also started to rebuild coverage. The encouraging point in that, the quality is our upcoming origination is significantly better. We expect a gradual improvement in asset quality, and impairments will take longer to normalize. On efficiency, we continue to make progress on our cost base. Our priority is to make these savings sustainable. As activity recovers, we should also benefit from operating leverage. Finally, on profitability, we expect to close 2026 with a similar ROE to the one reported for the first nine months of the year. Looking into 2027, we see several factors that should support a progressive recovery: higher business volumes, a lower impact from inflation accounting, continued cost discipline, and a gradual normalization of impairments.

    Sources indicate that we remain cautious about how quickly these factors will materialize. What is important is that we are facing this environment with a stronger competitive position and with a capital and liquidity to support future profitability and growth.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Anders Bylund – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 2:57PM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that growth-minded investors are currently weighing the rapid expansion of a Mediterranean dining star against the steady dominance of a global energy drink powerhouse.
    • According to recent reports, CAVA operates a fast-growing restaurant chain focusing on healthy, Mediterranean-inspired bowls and pitas.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Anders Bylund – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 2:57PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Cava Group ›.

    Recent findings suggest that growth-minded investors are currently weighing the rapid expansion of a Mediterranean dining star against the steady dominance of a global energy drink powerhouse. Choosing between CAVA Group (CAVA +2.02%) and Monster Beverage (MNST +1.02%) involves balancing high-octane growth with established cash flow.

    According to recent reports, CAVA operates a fast-growing restaurant chain focusing on healthy, Mediterranean-inspired bowls and pitas. Monster Beverage leads the energy drink market through a massive global distribution network. While one manufacturer is scaling a physical footprint across the country, the other is leveraging high net margins and a stable beverage portfolio to generate significant capital.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    CAVA serves chef-curated or build-your-own bowls and pitas at nearly 500 locations across the United States. The manufacturer emphasizes a multi-channel approach that includes in-restaurant dining, digital pick-up, and drive-thru options. It also sells branded dips and spreads in grocery stores, supporting its vertically-integrated supply chain of over 50 grower and producer partners.

    Industry observers note that expansion remains a central theme for the business as it enters upcoming states. In the 12 months ended Oct. 4, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.4 billion, representing 27% growth. The manufacturer reported net income of approximately $64.7 million for that same period, demonstrating its ability to maintain profitability while investing heavily in its growing store count.

    Industry observers note that the balance sheet appears robust enough to support its long-term goals for retail stocks. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.6x, a measure of financial leverage that compares total liabilities to shareholders' equity. A current ratio of 2.7x suggests the tech giant has sufficient assets to cover short-term liabilities, and in the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025, free cash flow was close to $26.1 million. Free cash flow is the cash remaining after a company pays for its physical investments and core business activities.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that monster Beverage develops and distributes energy drinks in roughly 80 countries worldwide. It relies heavily on a network of full-service beverage bottlers, including those within the Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) system. This distribution model allows the manufacturer to reach retail grocery chains, convenience stores, and e-commerce platforms with minimal direct capital investment in bottling facilities.

    Industry observers note that financial performance highlights the benefits of significant scale in the global beverage industry. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $9.6 billion, reflecting revenue growth of about 20.2%. For that period, the company recorded net income of roughly $2.2 billion, maintaining a healthy net margin of nearly 22.7%.

    The company maintains an exceptionally clean balance sheet to support its international expansion. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.0x, indicating that the firm carries no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio of 3.7x reveals a strong ability to meet short-term obligations, and in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $2.0 billion. Free cash flow is the cash that remains in the business after the company funds capital projects and core operations.

    CAVA faces intense competition within the restaurant and food manufacturing sectors from national players like Starbucks (SBUX +1.28%) and various local competitors. Expansion into fresh locations brings operational risks, including the challenge of maintaining brand culture and managing the costs of rapid growth. Furthermore, the firm depends on third-party delivery partners and faces potential food safety risks that could harm its brand reputation.

    According to recent reports, monster Beverage is heavily dependent on its relationship with distribution partners like Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP +0.57%). The organization faces stiff competition from global giants such as PepsiCo (PEP +0.88%) and emerging rivals like Celsius Holdings (CELH +1.86%). Recent write-downs in its alcohol segment also highlight risks related to product diversification and shifting consumer health perceptions regarding energy drinks.

    Monster Beverage appears more attractive based on its lower Forward P/E, while CAVA offers a lower P/S ratio despite its higher earnings multiple.

    Sources indicate that valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers. Data is current as of Nov. 24, 2026.

    Monster Beverage is the better pick over CAVA Group for 2027, though the two stocks suit different investors. I'm in Monster's corner, and it's not a close call.

    In a recent development, CAVA is the fun one. It has 500 restaurants, trailing revenue up 27%, a Las Vegas opening on deck, and a Mediterranean brand that makes lunch choices feel like a personality. It's hard not to root for it. But the latest quarter indicated same-restaurant sales up just 3.1%, net income down to $13.2 million from $14.7 million, and trailing free cash flow of only $39.1 million. And the stock, even after sliding from its highs, still trades as if everything will go right. Spoiler alert: that's a really rare long-term outcome.

    Monster is the grown-up in the room, if grown-ups sell caffeine bombs in neon cans. It posted $9.6 billion in trailing revenue, up 20.2%, along with $1.9 billion in free cash flow and zero debt. It doesn't need a cane to lean on if the economy limps. Coca-Cola's bottlers handle the heavy lifting on distribution, so the growth comes with minimal capital spending on Monster's end. That global partnership still has plenty of room to run.

    Sources indicate that investors who want a high-growth restaurant story can still make a case for CAVA. Those who want growth, strong cash generation, and a clean balance sheet have an easier choice. I would pass on CAVA at today's price and buy Monster stock instead.

    By Patrick Sanders – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

    Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks have taken a beating in November. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 index is down 15% this month on fears that AI spending has gotten out of hand. But the world's largest company seems immune to the problem.

    According to recent reports, smartphone maker Apple (AAPL +0.43%) is bucking the trend. Its shares are virtually unchanged for the month, and in 2026 it's posting generous gains, up more than 25%, while many of its AI peers slump.

    Recent findings suggest that and there's a good reason why. As other tech companies spend heavily on AI infrastructure, Apple is focused on bringing AI capabilities directly to its 2.5 billion devices at the moment in service.

    That strategy is looking pretty smart right now.

    Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are investing heavily in enormous cloud computing networks. Meta Platforms is working on "personal superintelligence," and Tesla is focused on robotics and Cybercabs.

    Apple's strategy, meanwhile, is focused on improving the experience for people who already own its smartphones, personal computers, tablets, and smart-home devices. Part of that strategy is integrating its devices with Siri AI, its improved personal assistant that launched this year. "Siri AI marks a fresh chapter in AI at Apple. It is a completely reimagined assistant that is powerful, personal, private, and deeply relevant to our owners' daily lives," CEO John Ternus mentioned.

    That's why it doesn't need to dominate the AI infrastructure business to benefit from artificial intelligence. It needs to give customers compelling reasons to buy another iPhone, Mac, or iPad.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Apple's financial results suggest that its core business remains exceptionally healthy.

    According to recent reports, it generated approximately $136 billion in free cash flow during fiscal 2026 (ended Sept. 26), up nearly 38% from the previous year. That's money remaining after capital expenditures, giving Apple tremendous flexibility to return cash to shareholders, invest in new products, and strengthen its business. Meanwhile, revenue jumped 15% to $478.8 billion for the fiscal year.

    Industry observers note that apple's balance sheet has allowed its stock to hold steady even as rising memory chip prices squeeze hardware margins. Management expects gross margins of 45% to 46% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, down from 47.9% in Q4 2026. But its services business, which carries gross margins of around 76%, provides an notable financial cushion.

    Apple has something that many AI infrastructure investors are still waiting to see from their investments: enormous cash generation without the same requirement to spend billions building the infrastructure that makes it possible.

    Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the upcoming season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

    Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a substantial challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

    It has been revealed that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about latest signings.

    “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he stated.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle mentioned he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    Sources indicate that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he remarked.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively upcoming corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • Industry observers note that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively upcoming corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    Industry observers note that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Sources indicate that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The firm posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    In a recent development, also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and confirmed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo noted.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".
