    Is Jensen Huang Really Worth $954 Billion to Nvidia?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) popped 31.5% on Monday, Nov.
    • The move came as Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director.
    • Investors may be wondering if one of roughly 42,000 employees should be worth such a large percentage of the company's value.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Foelber – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) popped 31.5% on Monday, Nov. 23. Nvidia closed with a market cap of $3.985 trillion -- $954 billion more than it closed at on Friday, Nov. 20. This would be the equivalent of creating the world's 16th most valuable tech giant out of thin air.

    The move came as Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director.

    Investors may be wondering if one of roughly 42,000 employees should be worth such a large percentage of the company's value.

    Here's why the move may still be an underreaction to how invaluable Huang is to Nvidia.

    It has been revealed that jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images.

    In a recent development, huang's sudden departure exposed serious threats to Nvidia's investment thesis -- namely, that management was ill-prepared to run the organization without him. And that the company's vision and culture centered on Huang.

    Huang ran the semiconductor manufacturer as an extension of himself, with dozens of direct reports and client relationships built on decades of industry experience. The informality of Nvidia's structure allowed Nvidia to operate with the speed of a start-up with the financial muscle of an industry leader -- which has been a lethal combination that has allowed Nvidia to fiercely protect its lead over the competition and maintain pricing power with high margins.

    Sources indicate that elon Musk, CEO of Tesla (TSLA -1.18%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%), has been one of the most public supporters for retaining Huang as CEO. In a conversation on the social media platform X, Elon Musk shed light on Huang's operating style and the vulnerabilities his departure created for Nvidia.

    If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through. Sure, we’d put together a purchase order at some point later, but I never for a second thought it wouldn’t happen.

    On SpaceX's second-quarter 2026 earnings call in August, which was its first earnings call as a public company, Musk mentioned that SpaceX would build exclusively on Nvidia because it believed that Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture was the best computing platform. With SpaceX owning xAI and having aims to build orbital constellations of AI compute satellites in space, being exclusive to Nvidia is a massive vote of confidence in Nvidia's innovation. But also in Jensen Huang.

    In a recent development, I doubt Musk would make such a clear commitment if he didn't believe in Nvidia's tech just as much as he does in its leadership. And if Huang were to leave and Nvidia's future computing platforms didn't produce as big a leap as Rubin did from Blackwell, or as big a leap as Blackwell did compared to Hopper, then Nvidia could be leaving business from top innovators like SpaceX on the table.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    In the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, Nvidia reported a 103% year-over-year increase in quarterly revenue and a generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) gross margin of 74.8%. Nvidia is at the moment in its fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. But management is already guiding for a 75% increase in year-over-year revenue in fiscal 2028 -- up from prior guidance of 70%.

    Nvidia spent years developing Rubin but only began shipments in August. In Nvidia's latest quarter, Rubin contributed nearly $20 billion in revenue compared to $107.6 billion in total data center revenue, which made it the fastest product ramp-up in history in a product's first quarter of shipments.

    It has been revealed that there are few CEOs as intertwined with a manufacturer's investment thesis as tech founders like Jensen Huang with Nvidia, Elon Musk with Tesla and SpaceX, and Mark Zuckerberg with Meta Platforms (META +3.40%). It's clear that Huang's ability to drive innovation and multi-year commitments is an inseparable element of Nvidia's valuation. So while Huang is definitely worth at least $954 billion to Nvidia, his sudden resignation exposed a gaping hole in Nvidia's investment thesis that needs to be plugged with a clear succession plan and improved governance.

    It has been revealed that there's also the ongoing risk that internal and external investigations expose facts that force Huang to resign down the road. Pay close attention to the wording of the Nov. 23 press release -- that Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk. I take that to mean that Huang's return as CEO isn't a national security threat, not that Huang is totally in the clear on national security leaks and export violations.

    Until investors get more clarity, Nvidia remains a hold rather than a buy.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Oracle (ORCL -5.13%) stock was down by more than 8% at midday today.
    • Sources indicate that the weakening sentiment is evident in the credit default swap (CDS) pricing on its debt.
    • In the middle of 2025, the CDS on Oracle's 5-year debt stood at just 35 bps, but it closed out 2025 at 154 bps.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lee Samaha – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:20PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Oracle ›.

    Oracle (ORCL -5.13%) stock was down by more than 8% at midday today. The slump comes on a day of weakness for AI -related stocks. In a nutshell, there are increasing concerns around the costs of AI enterprises developing frontier AI models and, in turn, their ability to pay AI infrastructure companies like Oracle.

    Sources indicate that the weakening sentiment is evident in the credit default swap (CDS) pricing on its debt. CDS pricing reflects thre price of insuring against a debt default. It's measured in basis points (bps), whereby 100 basis points equals 1%. So, for example, insuring $1 million in debt with a CDS at 100 bps (1%) would cost $10,000 per year.

    In the middle of 2025, the CDS on Oracle's 5-year debt stood at just 35 bps, but it closed out 2025 at 154 bps. But here's the thing. Yesterday it spiked to 360 bps, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.

    Industry observers note that to put that number into context, the bond market typically assumes that 40% of a defaulted bond is actually paid out, so the implied annual hazard rate can be calculated by dividing the CDS price by the 60% loss in default. In other words, .036/0.6=.06, or 6% a year.

    Recent findings suggest that over 5 years, the cumulative rate equates to almost 26%. While it's notable to note this is just the bond market pricing, there is still a lot of fear in the market over Oracle. Those fears are centered on its soaring capital expenditures to fund its AI build-out, which have turned its cash flow negative.

    ORCL Free Cash Flow data by YCharts.

    Meanwhile, Oracle's debt has soared.

    ORCL Net Total Long Term Debt (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

    The market is clearly worried about the sustainability of AI investment, and in such conditions it makes sense to focus on stronger players like Alphabet on weakness, rather than chase Oracle stock.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Chris Neiger – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:33PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) made headlines recently because of its blockbuster IPO, and investors are still trying to decide how the newly public artificial intelligence (AI) company will impact the broader AI market.

    In a recent development, some of the details Anthropic disclosed in its S-1 filing before going public shed light on its potential impact, especially on chip companies. Anthropic presently has deals with multiple chip companies to help provide the compute capacity it needs for its AI services.

    It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) is, unsurprisingly, a key supplier of chips to Anthropic, but so are Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%) (GOOG -2.02%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -1.75%). Instead of tying itself to just one chip organization, Anthropic has decided to spread out its chip vendors.

    That could change Nvidia's growth narrative in the coming years. Here's how it's shifting and why Nvidia investors don't need to panic just yet.

    In a recent development, between cloud computing contracts and chip deals, Anthropic is on the hook for about $900 billion in spending over the next several years. That's a heck of a lot of money to spend, and Anthropic hopes it will accelerate its sales far beyond the organization's current annual revenue run rate of $81 billion.

    It's also far too much money to funnel toward just one or two AI infrastructure companies. To minimize its supply chain risks, ensure it has the most advanced technology, and negotiate better chip prices, Anthropic spreads its chip deals across four key players.

    Here are Anthropic's biggest AI chip deals:.

    While Anthropic doesn't disclose all the details of each deal, including how much they might be worth, this data highlights that Anthropic is clearly hedging its bets when it comes to buying AI chips.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    According to recent reports, nvidia's GPUs are still among the most in-demand chips in the world, and they're very likely to remain so for years to come due to AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had an estimated 80%-90% market share of AI accelerators last year and is estimated to have 75% this year.

    That's both good and bad news for Nvidia. Having three-quarters of the AI accelerator market is huge, and it's part of the reason why Nvidia just reported another impressive quarter, with Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue rising 103% to $115.8 billion and earnings per share jumping 111% to $2.68.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that but AMD's GPUs and custom silicon from Google, Broadcom, and Amazon are reducing Nvidia's dominance. Part of the reason is that custom chips (like the ones Anthropic buys from Nvidia rivals) are good at handling agentic AI tasks and are more efficient than the raw processing power from GPUs.

    Industry observers note that what's more, Nvidia's gross margins, while still high, are declining. The company remarked gross margins will be between 71% and 72% in the fourth quarter, down from nearly 75% in the third quarter. This downward pressure is mostly coming from rising memory costs right now, but intensifying chip competition could weigh on margins further in the coming years.

    According to recent reports, still, while Nvidia shareholders should be aware of how rival chip companies could impact the tech giant over time, Nvidia is still the leading AI accelerator company. Its recent revenue guidance for 75% growth in the fourth quarter -- up from its previous guidance of 70% -- should reassure investors that the company isn't getting sidelined anytime soon.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:47PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    Investors can't help but think about the 2026 performance of a popular defensive name. The S&P 500, with heavy exposure to technology and artificial intelligence, is only up 6% this year (as of Nov. 23). Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%), on the other hand, has soared 37%.

    The beverage stock isn't known for its growth potential, which has been a pleasant surprise in 2026. Instead, investors choose to buy and hold this industry-leading company because it's a safe choice that can generate a healthy dividend stream.

    Coca-Cola has raised its dividend payout for a mind-blowing 64 straight years, making it a Dividend King, or a company that has raised its payout for 50 years or more. Purchasing $10,000 worth of its shares today will bring in this much passive income in 2027.

    Coca-Cola's board of directors approved a roughly 4% dividend hike on Feb. 19. The quarterly payout climbed from $0.51 to $0.53 per share, or $2.12 annualized.

    Recent findings suggest that today's annual payout is 51% higher than the $1.40 per share paid in 2016. That's about 4.2% annualized growth. It isn't spectacular. But it's consistent, surviving a pandemic and a bout of high inflation.

    Sources indicate that here's the math investors care about. Buying $10,000 at the current share price of $95.88 gets you 104 shares. Based on today's payout, that position would generate more than $220 in dividend income in 2027. If the board delivers another raise in February, a near certain event, that figure will obviously be higher.

    In a recent development, the dividend yield sits at 2.21%. The S&P 500 yields just 1.12%. Consequently, $10,000 in an S&P 500 index fund would produce only about $112 a year. Coca-Cola nearly doubles that.

    According to recent reports, there's a catch, though. Coca-Cola yielded 2.66% the day after its February raise. This stock's impressive rally this year has pushed the yield much lower. Income investors are now paying more for every dollar of dividends.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that nobody questions the quality of this business. Coca-Cola sells drinks in more than 200 countries and territories. Its flagship trademark is the world's most valuable food and beverage brand, according to Kantar.

    That brand strength translates into durable pricing power. In the third quarter, net revenue grew 7% year over year to $13.4 billion. Unit case volume, a measure of how much product consumers bought, jumped 5%. Yet price/mix (higher prices plus a richer product mix) still added 1%. Coca-Cola sold more without sacrificing price.

    Profitability improved. The comparable operating margin, which excludes one-time items, widened to 32.9% from 31.9%. Comparable earnings per share (EPS) rose 11% to $0.91, beating Wall Street's $0.88 estimate. Management now expects full-year comparable EPS growth of at least 11%.

    Valuation is the problem. Coca-Cola trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 28.3. The S&P 500's index's P/E multiple is 20.3. That's a 39% premium for a company that isn't built for speed.

    In a recent development, management's long-term targets call for 4% to 5% organic revenue growth (excluding currency and acquisitions). Sell-side analysts expect the top line to shrink in 2027.

    Industry observers note that this year's gain was less about profits. The stock's 37% surge far outpaces that 11% earnings outlook for the year. Investors simply paid more for each dollar of earnings, with the P/E ratio rising 23% in 2026. That can't continue indefinitely.

    According to recent reports, I wouldn't buy Coca-Cola at today's price. With the best outcome being mid- to high-single-digit growth ahead, the valuation leaves little room for upside. Patient investors who appreciate the dividend should wait for a cheaper entry point.

    • Recent findings suggest that as mobile markets mature and artificial intelligence expands, investors are looking for the next major chip winner.
    • Qualcomm provides the wireless connectivity and processors that power modern smartphones and connected vehicles.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 4:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Qualcomm ›.

    Recent findings suggest that as mobile markets mature and artificial intelligence expands, investors are looking for the next major chip winner. Is Qualcomm (QCOM +2.24%) or Sandisk (SNDK -5.57%) the better choice for your 2027 portfolio?

    Qualcomm provides the wireless connectivity and processors that power modern smartphones and connected vehicles. Sandisk specializes in the flash storage and memory solutions required for high-speed data processing in cloud environments. Both companies are essential to the global technology infrastructure, but they offer vastly different financial profiles for investors to consider.

    Sources indicate that as one of the most prominent semiconductor stocks, Qualcomm designs the high-performance computing and connectivity platforms found in premium handsets and industrial devices. The firm relies on a small group of mobile handset customers, including Apple Inc. (AAPL +0.43%) and Samsung, for a significant portion of its revenue. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, particularly as Apple develops its own internal modem technology. To offset this, Qualcomm is expanding into automotive and data center markets while partnering with Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%) to provide radio platforms for the Starlink Mobile 5G network.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached about $43.1 billion, representing a decrease of approximately 2.6% compared to the previous twelve-month period. Despite the slight revenue dip, the company reported a net income of roughly $13.6 billion for that time frame. Net margin for the year was about 32%, showing the company's ability to maintain high profitability even during a period of slowing top-line growth.

    The manufacturer maintains a solid balance sheet, with a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.5x as of its September 2026 balance sheet. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity, indicating the company maintains a manageable level of borrowing. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, stands at nearly 1.9x. For the fiscal year ended Sept. 27, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $8.7 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 31% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    According to recent reports, sandisk operates as a major force in the flash memory industry, serving the massive data center, PC, and mobile device markets. The tech giant provides the hardware necessary for storing and moving the vast amounts of data used by modern artificial intelligence systems. Unlike many chip peers, its sales are highly diverse, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue in the most recent fiscal year. This broad base of OEM and channel customers helps reduce the impact of any single partnership ending.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached about $29 billion, a significant growth of approximately 272% over the prior year. This rapid expansion was accompanied by a net income of roughly $19.4 billion. The surge in sales and earnings reflects the intense demand for high-capacity memory solutions in the cloud computing sector. The company achieved a net margin of nearly 67% during this period, highlighting the strong demand for its memory technology.

    It has been revealed that as of July 2026, the company reported a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, indicating that total liabilities do not exceed shareholder equity and its reliance on debt is minimal. Its current ratio was nearly 2.3x, suggesting a comfortable cushion for meeting its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $11.5 billion. This robust cash generation allows the company to reinvest heavily in manufacturing facilities and next-generation storage research.

    Qualcomm faces significant risks from its revenue concentration among a small number of handset manufacturers. The company expects Apple will transition to its own internally developed modems in the near future, which could impact sales. Furthermore, heavy exposure to the Chinese market makes the company vulnerable to shifting trade policies and national security regulations. Its reliance on a fabless model also means it depends on third-party foundries like Taiwan Semiconductor and Samsung for leading-edge production capacity.

    Sandisk carries operational risks due to its heavy reliance on joint ventures with Kioxia for memory production. Its manufacturing facilities are geographically concentrated in Japan and Malaysia, leaving the supply chain open to disruption from natural disasters or geopolitical conflict. The memory industry is also notoriously cyclical, with intense competition from Nvidia Corp. (NVDA -3.91%), Western Digital (WDC -0.55%), and Micron Technology (MU -4.53%). The company must also manage the complexities associated with its separation from Western Digital, including potential tax liabilities.

    Sandisk appears significantly cheaper based on future earnings estimates, while Qualcomm maintains a slightly higher premium for its diversified connectivity portfolio.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    Sources indicate that qualcomm's mobile phone business has been hammered this year, as weak Chinese demand and AI-driven memory shortages have caused handset-derived sales to fall below prior-year levels. Yet the AI boom has an upside for Qualcomm.

    At the manufacturer's June 2026 investor day, Qualcomm raised its non-handset revenue target to more than $40 billion by 2029, nearly double the prior target of $22 billion. Qualcomm is reportedly partnering with OpenAI to develop smartphone processors with advanced AI capabilities. Analysts see this partnership as a positive for Qualcomm since it would enable advanced agentic AI on smartphone platforms. It would also diminish the business risk of Apple developing its own chips and dropping Qualcomm as a supplier.

    Meanwhile, Sandisk shares have undergone remarkable appreciation since its spin-off from Western Digital created the firm as a stand-alone entity in February 2025. Shares went from $49 to more than $2,300 by the middle of 2026. Shares have since undergone an 8-for-1 split and seen a significant retracement of gains.

    Sources indicate that but the share strength shows just how strong the flash memory market has been for Sandisk. During periods of tight supply and strong market pricing, the tech giant's profit margins can be robust, as they have been during this AI-driven market. Historically, though, high memory prices and low supply are followed by periods of high supply and low prices, which are a risk to Sandisk investors in the long run.

    Recent findings suggest that still, the growth is impressive. Revenue should get near $50 billion 2027, more than double 2026, with Wall Street seeing more than $60 billion in sales in 2028. Net income should triple in 2027, to $34.9 billion, and grow more modestly in 2028.

    The choice here is simply: Sandisk is booming and comes at a bargain-basement valuation while Qualcomm's expected improvement is still speculative at the moment. There is risk to Sandisk that one may be buying at the peak of the memory cycle, but it's clearly the better bet for 2027.

The proof of that is that it is the only Dividend King real estate investment trust (REIT). You don't string together 50+ annual dividend increases by accident; it requires a strong business model that is executed well in both good times and bad.

    Sources indicate that federal Realty's approach is actually pretty simple. It buys properties surrounded by lots of wealthy customers. Then it redevelops the assets to ensure they are attractive to both consumers and tenants, including carefully curating the tenant list. When a property reaches full value, the REIT sells it and starts again with a new asset. That approach isn't particularly shocking, but it is hard to execute well. Federal Realty's dividend track record demonstrates it consistently executes well.

    According to recent reports, you can find higher-yielding REITs pretty easily, but there's only one REIT that can claim to be a Dividend King. For conservative dividend investors, Federal Realty's well-above-market 4.2% yield should help you sleep well at night, even when the market gets turbulent. And since the world is increasingly moving toward digital transactions, where paper money isn't an option, Visa is likely to have years of growth ahead. It is a very real problem, but Pfizer is actively working on its pipeline to offset the revenue hit. Only, drug development doesn't work on a schedule, even though patent expirations do.

Moreover, the company continues to stand behind not only supporting the dividend at its current level, but growing it over time.     #108076. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (752 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the manufacturer's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Industry observers note that huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate latest multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider stated in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Sources indicate that tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    It has been revealed that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The tech giant had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Industry observers note that neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, remarked CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he mentioned.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    In a recent development, bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any massive changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real matter is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    According to recent reports, "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he stated. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Stefon Walters – Nov 25, 2026 at 4:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF ›.

    An extra $500 monthly has a nice ring to it. It could cover a couple of bills, a few grocery store runs, or simply sit in your savings for a rainy day. Either way, bringing in $500 monthly with no extra work is hard to beat.

    Industry observers note that there are plenty of dividend stocks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) to choose from, but I'm a fan of the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD +1.15%) because it's a trifecta: diversified, high-yield, and cheap. It's a dividend ETF you can trust and treat as a set-it-and-forget-it investment.

    SCHD only holds 102 stocks, but they're well-established and vetted for quality. To be included in the fund, a company needs to be in good financial standing, have paid dividends for at least 10 years, and have increased its annual dividend for at least five years. Of course, some of its holdings can hit rough patches (as every company does), but those that check those boxes are usually built to last.

    Recent findings suggest that SCHD's holdings include 11 Dividend Kings (companies with at least 50 consecutive years of dividend increases), including four in its top 10 holdings: Procter & Gamble, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, and Abbott Laboratories. Together, these four account for over 17% of the ETF, and Dividend Kings account for over 27% (as of Nov. 23).

    SCHD can be a good complement to investing in the S&P 500 because it's not as tech-heavy as the index or many other popular indexes and ETFs. Most of its holdings come from more "boring" sectors like consumer staples (19.97%), healthcare (19.20%), and energy (15.38%).

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Recent findings suggest that dividend yields move in the opposite direction of stock prices, so SCHD's 25% surge this year (as of Nov. 23) has pushed its yield down a bit. At the time of writing, its yield is 3.1%, which is below its average over the past three years, but it's still one of the highest yields you'll find in a major dividend ETF or blue chip dividend stocks.

    SCHD Dividend Yield data by YCharts.

    In a recent development, since SCHD is an ETF, its quarterly payouts aren't as straightforward as individual stocks. When Coca-Cola, for example, sets an annual dividend of $2.12, you know you'll get four $0.53 payouts. SCHD's holdings pay dividends at different times, so SCHD's payout fluctuates. But based on yields, here is how much you'd need invested to generate $500 monthly ($6,000 annually):.

    Generating $500 monthly from SCHD won't happen overnight for most investors, but it's an ETF you can comfortably add to over time and trust to compound toward your target. Ideally, you'd reinvest your dividends to buy more SCHD shares and speed up the process. The earlier you start, the better.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aaron Rodgers' time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has about to officially come to an end following his benching and comments on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".
    • Sources indicate that according to Jordan Schultz and Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac, the team will be releasing the soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback once his contract situation is finalized.
    • The situation went from the Steelers announcing late Tuesday evening that Rodgers would be benched to him airing his feelings about Mike McCarthy less than 24 hours later.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aaron Rodgers' time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has about to officially come to an end following his benching and comments on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    Sources indicate that according to Jordan Schultz and Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac, the team will be releasing the soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback once his contract situation is finalized. Rodgers signed a one-year, $22.5 million deal in May.

    The situation went from the Steelers announcing late Tuesday evening that Rodgers would be benched to him airing his feelings about Mike McCarthy less than 24 hours later.

    On "McAfee," Rodgers claimed that McCarthy fell asleep and snored during a quarterbacks meeting after arriving late. He also said that the Steelers head coach broke down the team during halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles by saying, "Alright, 1-2-3-Packers!".

    The four-time NFL MVP added that he found out he was being benched in favor of Mason Rudolph from Steelers' tight end Pat Freiermuth.

    "I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he mentioned, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know," Rodgers said. "And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn't hear from Mike [McCarthy].".

    "Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up.".

    Recent findings suggest that what comes next for Rodgers? That's to be determined. He noted on "McAfee" that the "ship has sailed" in regards to a return to the Steelers. Now, he will be free agent once he clear waivers.

    Rodgers had already declared in May that the 2026 season would be his last in the NFL.

    In 10 games this season, Rodgers has thrown for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

    #108062. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    📅 13 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4879 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

    📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4879 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
    • Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
    • Industry observers note that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the significant positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    Industry observers note that signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    Sources indicate that emery remarked: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    Industry observers note that “Of course there is still work to do but they indicated they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    Recent findings suggest that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    Sources indicate that the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Sources indicate that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    According to recent reports, it was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    In a recent development, before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    It has been revealed that PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    According to recent reports, villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    It has been revealed that it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

    After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

    PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

    It has been revealed that both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

    Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

    💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

    Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season.

    PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

    Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

    Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

    Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

    PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

    Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

    Into the final minute of added time we go.

    Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

    There will be five added minutes.

    Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

    According to recent reports, one final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

    Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

    According to recent reports, the ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

    Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

    Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

    Sources indicate that PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

    In a recent development, aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

    The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

    We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

    Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

    Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

    The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

    Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

    It has been revealed that mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

    Industry observers note that other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

    Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

    One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

    It has been revealed that two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

    Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

    We are back under way in Salzburg.

    Brian Madjo - remember the name.

    Sources indicate that incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

    Sources indicate that the teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

    Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

    Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17.

    After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

    On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    In a recent development, madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

    Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes concerns for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

    Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

    Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

    Sources indicate that hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

    Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly upcoming rules that will be good for the game.

    It has been revealed that A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

    Brian Madjo with a significant chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    According to recent reports, after Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

    Sources indicate that PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

    Industry observers note that A few minutes after I stated that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

    Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

    Recent findings suggest that moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

    In a recent development, in last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

    This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

    Recent findings suggest that mcGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

    Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

    We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

    Recent findings suggest that some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:.

    PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

    Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

    It has been revealed that 💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo.

    Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

    PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

    Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

    It has been revealed that “There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”.

    INS:Johan Manzambi ⇠ Freiburg, £50mJoao Gomes ⇠ Wolves, £34mAlejandro Garnacho ⇠ Chelsea, LoanModou Keba Cisse ⇠ LASK, £5m.

    OUTS:Youri Tielemans ⇢ Manchester United, £36mDonyell Malen ⇢ Roma, £20mMorgan Rogers ⇢ Chelsea, £117mLewis Dobbin ⇢ Southampton, £10mEnzo Barrenechea ⇢ Benfica, £10mLucas Digne ⇢ PSG, £8mEvann Guessand ⇢ Crystal Palace, Loan.

    2025- PSG 2 Tottenham 2 (Udine, PSG won on penalties)2024- Real Madrid 2 Atalanta 0 (Poland)2023- Manchester City 1 Sevilla 1 (Athens, Manchester City won on penalties)2022- Real Madrid 2 Eintracht Frankfurt 0 (Helsinki)2021- Chelsea 1 Villarreal 1 (Belfast, Chelsea won on penalties).

    Latest Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

    Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

    Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

    Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ.

    Recent findings suggest that what will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    Sources indicate that unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    Industry observers note that I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Industry observers note that aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a substantial summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    Recent findings suggest that “I feel like the club is in a fresh era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    Industry observers note that PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    In a recent development, “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.
